scenes.visual: THE WORLD, kept for both chapters (16:9, dark navy background). A Punnett grid of equal square BOXES drawn in thin WHITE lines; allele letters sit on the grid edges in WHITE; each box holds a LABEL chip coloured by phenotype: PURPLE for purple, RED for red, PINK for pink, pale GREY for white, YELLOW for yellow coat, near-BLACK with a white outline for black coat. A box whose label is 'dies' goes dark and its outline dashes. Ratios always appear on screen as text, never only spoken. Title card 'Same Boxes, New Labels' fades in over an empty 2x2 grid.

scenes.tts: Why does a yellow mouse never breed true? Mate two yellow mice again and again, and black pups keep turning up. One litter may be all yellow by chance. But no yellow line ever stays yellow.
scenes.visual: A yellow mouse pair at left. A litter appears below them: YELLOW pups with about a third BLACK. A second litter drops in, all YELLOW by chance; a third has BLACK pups again. A counter 'true-breeding yellow lines: 0' stays at zero.
scenes.narration: Why does a yellow mouse never breed true? Mate two yellow mice again and again, and black pups keep turning up. One litter may be all yellow by chance. But no yellow line ever stays yellow.

scenes.tts: That looked like a failure of Mendel's rules. It was not. It was a clue that inheritance works in two layers.
scenes.visual: A tag 'Lucien Cuénot, mouse crosses, early 1900s' at top. The words 'Mendel failed?' appear, then are struck through. Two stacked bands slide in, labelled 'layer 1: the deal' and 'layer 2: the labels'.
scenes.narration: That looked like a failure of Mendel's rules. It was not. It was a clue that inheritance works in two layers.

scenes.tts: The first layer is the deal. At meiosis, each parent's two alleles separate into different gametes. So each child gets one allele from each parent.
scenes.visual: Two parent cells, each with two allele tokens (one capital, one small). At 'separate', each cell splits into two gametes with one token each. Arrows bring one gamete from each parent together into a child.
scenes.narration: The first layer is the deal. At meiosis, each parent's two alleles separate into different gametes. So each child gets one allele from each parent.

scenes.tts: Cross two parents that carry the same two alleles, one copy of each. Each parent passes on either allele equally often, and gametes meet at random. So the pairings fill four equally likely boxes. One box gets two of the first allele. Two boxes get one of each. One box gets two of the second.
scenes.visual: The gametes line the top and side of the 2x2 grid, each with '1/2' beside it and a small tag 'fair deal: equal transmission, random meeting'. Each box fills with its genotype in WHITE: AA, Aa, Aa, aa, lighting as named. Below the grid: '1 : 2 : 1'.
scenes.narration: Cross two parents that carry the same two alleles, one copy of each. Each parent passes on either allele equally often, and gametes meet at random. So the pairings fill four equally likely boxes. One box gets two of the first allele. Two boxes get one of each. One box gets two of the second.

scenes.tts: That deal is the part Mendel got right. It never changes in this chapter. What changes is the label written in each box.
scenes.visual: A padlock icon settles on the grid's lines with the word 'deal: fixed'. Four empty label chips float above the boxes, waiting.
scenes.narration: That deal is the part Mendel got right. It never changes in this chapter. What changes is the label written in each box.

scenes.tts: In Mendel's peas, one purple allele is enough. A plant with one purple allele is as purple as a plant with two. So three boxes share one label. That is Mendel's familiar ratio.
scenes.visual: A pea flower icon. Three boxes (AA, Aa, Aa) take PURPLE chips, the aa box a pale GREY chip. The three purple chips merge into one bracket labelled 'purple'. Below: '3 : 1'.
scenes.narration: In Mendel's peas, one purple allele is enough. A plant with one purple allele is as purple as a plant with two. So three boxes share one label. That is Mendel's familiar ratio.

scenes.tts: Snapdragons write the labels differently. Cross red with white, and every child is pink. In a snapdragon, one red allele gives only a pink flower.
scenes.visual: The chips clear; the grid stays. A RED snapdragon and a GREY-white snapdragon at the top; a PINK flower appears below them, labelled 'every F1 plant'.
scenes.narration: Snapdragons write the labels differently. Cross red with white, and every child is pink. In a snapdragon, one red allele gives only a pink flower.

scenes.tts: Now let the pink plants pollinate themselves. Red and white come back. Each box keeps its own label. Nothing blended.
scenes.visual: The same 2x2 grid fills: RED chip in AA, PINK in both Aa boxes, GREY-white in aa. No chips merge. Below: '1 red : 2 pink : 1 white'. A small struck-through word 'blending' fades.
scenes.narration: Now let the pink plants pollinate themselves. Red and white come back. Each box keeps its own label. Nothing blended.

scenes.tts: Now the yellow mouse. One yellow allele is enough to make the coat yellow. Mate two yellow mice, and the same four boxes appear.
scenes.visual: Chips clear. Mouse icons replace the flowers. Gametes on the edges read 'yellow' and 'black allele'. The two mixed boxes take YELLOW chips, the box with two black alleles a BLACK chip. The box with two yellow alleles stays empty, glowing faintly.
scenes.narration: Now the yellow mouse. One yellow allele is enough to make the coat yellow. Mate two yellow mice, and the same four boxes appear.

scenes.tts: So what label goes in the box with two yellow alleles?
scenes.visual: The empty box pulses. A question card: 'Two yellow alleles: what label?'
scenes.narration: So what label goes in the box with two yellow alleles?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. The question card stays; the empty box pulses slowly. A 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: That label is death. Two copies of the yellow allele kill the embryo very early, before implantation. So that box goes dark and drops out of the count.
scenes.visual: The card dissolves. The empty box takes a chip reading 'dies', then goes dark; its outline turns dashed. The three remaining boxes slide slightly together.
scenes.narration: That label is death. Two copies of the yellow allele kill the embryo very early, before implantation. So that box goes dark and drops out of the count.

scenes.tts: So among live pups, yellow outnumbers black by the ratio on screen. And every yellow pup is a heterozygote, with one yellow allele and one other.
scenes.visual: Below the grid: '2 yellow : 1 black (among live pups)'. Both YELLOW boxes highlight with their genotype shown: one yellow allele plus one black allele. The word 'heterozygote' appears beside them.
scenes.narration: So among live pups, yellow outnumbers black by the ratio on screen. And every yellow pup is a heterozygote, with one yellow allele and one other.

scenes.tts: That is why no yellow mouse breeds true. Two heterozygotes always deal some boxes with no yellow allele at all.
scenes.visual: Return to the yellow pair and their litter from the opening; the black pups now point to the BLACK box with a thin line.
scenes.narration: That is why no yellow mouse breeds true. Two heterozygotes always deal some boxes with no yellow allele at all.

scenes.tts: So here is the idea. Inheritance deals the boxes. What each allele's product does writes the labels. Some boxes share a label, some keep their own, and one can be labelled dies.
scenes.visual: The three grids (pea, snapdragon, mouse) shrink and sit side by side. The words appear one line at a time: 'Inheritance deals the boxes.' 'The gene products write the labels.' Under each grid in turn: 'share a label', 'keep their own', 'dies: dropped'.
scenes.narration: So here is the idea. Inheritance deals the boxes. What each allele's product does writes the labels. Some boxes share a label, some keep their own, and one can be labelled dies.

scenes.tts: This holds while the deal is fair, the genes are unlinked, and each box gets one label. When a genotype gives only a chance of a trait, the rule stops.
scenes.visual: A thin WHITE frame draws around the three grids with a small tag 'scope: fair deal, unlinked genes, one label per box'. At the frame's edge a faint dotted line marks 'where the rule stops: a box with only a chance of a label'.
scenes.narration: This holds while the deal is fair, the genes are unlinked, and each box gets one label. When a genotype gives only a chance of a trait, the rule stops.

scenes.visual: End card over the dimmed grids, large white text, centred: 'Inheritance deals the boxes; the gene products write the labels.'
